cells.tense: The exchange between you and the world runs close to even right now.
cells.act: keep what the change produced from drifting
cells.ask: Something you started recently — a shared habit, a rebuilt plan, a way of splitting costs — is in decent shape. Leave it where it stands. Don't improve it, don't give it up, don't touch it at all this month.
cells.core:
Giving and receiving are running about even for you now, and it shows. What you put out comes back without a ledger, and the weight of what's fair isn't something you carry around. That steadiness lives in your body, in the ordinary exchanges of your week, and it holds because it isn't being held up by effort.

There's a draw in you toward what you actually want, and it feels true rather than strained, because the ground under it is even. So don't rush the next version. Something you started recently — a shared habit, a rebuilt plan, a way of splitting costs — is in decent shape. Leave it where it stands, this month. Don't improve it, don't give it up. Keeping the good part in place is the work here, and it's real work.
cells.sheetLine: The exchange runs even, and your body knows it.
cells.verb: give and take in even measure
cells.place: in the pull toward the light you steer by

cells.tense: You are watching the scales so closely that the giving has stopped being exchange.
cells.ask: Take one shared thing you've been evening out — the bills, the visits, the running of something — and keep it level on your own for a stretch. Ask nothing back. Decide nothing new. See whether it stands without your hand on it.
cells.core:
You want the accounts to balance, and the checking has gotten out in front of the actual exchange. You look at whether you've given enough, whether you'll get your share, whether things landed fair — and you brace for a moment that hasn't come, so you push a little harder to make sure it does. What used to move between you and people moves in your head first now.

There is a quiet strength in you that can hold a load without watching anyone else's hands. Take one shared thing you've been evening out — the bills, the visits, the running of something — and keep it level, alone, for a stretch. Ask nothing back, decide nothing new. See whether it stands without your hand on it. You'll learn something from the stretch either way.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing for a fair moment that hasn't arrived.

cells.tense: You have stopped putting toward the light, and the giving that once came easily is behind you now.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Where the exchange ran thin — one friend, one shared task, one habit of giving — take an unhurried hour and sort what that connection asks of you now from what it asked of you once. Two columns, one sheet.
cells.core:
Something that used to flow between you and other people has gone quiet. You're not giving much now, and you're not asking, and what you really want feels far off — like a door you were already past when you noticed it. Nothing is charged under the light you steer by, so nothing turns toward it, however much you'd like it to. That isn't a failure of feeling. It's that what used to feed it has run thin.

So don't try to want something more, and don't push generosity you don't have. Sharpen the eye instead. Where the exchange ran thin — one friend, one shared task, one habit of giving — take an unhurried hour and sort what that connection asks of you now from what it asked of you once. Two columns, one sheet. Attention like that feeds the light back, slowly.
cells.sheetLine: What used to flow between you and others has gone quiet.

cells.tense: You are giving and taking in a way you haven't yet given your own name to.
cells.act: weigh what you know before it leaves you
cells.ask: When something lands, and it touches someone else, sit with it a day before you act. No announcement. No reasoning it through. Then act on what still stands.
cells.core:
You keep things fair without thinking about it much. You notice who's short, who's owed, where the balance slipped, and you adjust — and if someone described you that way you'd likely shrug and say you were just getting along, being sensible about time and money. Meanwhile the light ahead, the thing you actually want, steers you more than that story does. It shows in what you choose when nobody asks why.

What you know about a situation arrives quietly and proves more right than the reasons you build afterward. Trust it before you argue with it. When something lands, and it touches someone else, sit with it for a day before you act. No announcement, no reasoning it through. Then act on what still stands. It'll be steadier for the wait, and shorter.
cells.sheetLine: You keep things even and give it no weight.
cells.verb: give and take in even measure
cells.place: in the pull toward the light you steer by
